title: Embed local destination bodies for community inclusion

blocks.text: The first enabling theme covers who benefits from growth, how it is paid for and how it lasts. It holds three focus areas: community inclusion, climate risk and investment. The inclusion entry stays at concept level, as agreed with Wesgro on 24 September 2026; roles and funding sit in Chapter 4.
Theme 3.1 · Investment, inclusion and sustainability · Focus area 13
Embed local destination bodies for community inclusion

Twenty communities hold 18.4% of the province's residents but receive only a small documented share of foreign direct spend, and in eleven the binding constraint is organisation, not distance or product.
**December 2025.** Drive Community and SME Inclusion (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p64).

**October 2026: Refined.** A seller with a stake, 20 communities and R259m at 1%. The SME and Community Inclusion Plan drove the refinement. As agreed with Wesgro on 24 September 2026, the entry stays at concept level, and roles and funding are set in Chapter 4.

blocks.caption: The shortlisted communities sit close to visitors but earn almost nothing from them, and most lack a body that can sell.
blocks.source: SME and Community Inclusion Plan, Sep 2026 (SCIP; desk research 17 to 23 September 2026, ratings from the community side with LTO confirmation outstanding). The R259m is 1% of the R25.9bn FY2025 foreign direct spend in the Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p11. The plan does not describe how the spend floor was traced. The multiple of today's floor is computed.
rows: 93 of 107 long-listed communities lie within 45 minutes of a tourism node or corridor; distance is the binding constraint in none of the 20
18.4% of residents (Census 2011) against a traced floor of 0.02% to 0.04% of foreign direct spend, about R4m to R10m a year
Organisation is the binding constraint in 11 of 20 communities, and 10 have no identified active tourism body
No profiled community rates Ready on digital and bookability; Zwelihle's four resident guides sell by phone with no shared channel
9 of 20 communities record a safety-perception gap and 5 record extortion (SAPS 2025/26 station data)
1% of FY2025 foreign direct spend is R259m a year, about 26 to 65 times today's documented floor

blocks.text: [Open item: the Inclusion Plan to set out how the R4m to R10m floor was traced.]

The plan's five cases set the order of action: a seller with a stake, a safe and workable visit, product that keeps spend in the community, then exposure (SME and Community Inclusion Plan, Sep 2026, p12). Kliptown in Soweto shows the cost of the reverse order. Walter Sisulu Square cost R160 million to R180 million, out of the R436 million first allocated to Kliptown (section 2.6), before an operator was in place, and drew about 4,000 museum visitors a year by 2017 against a business case of almost 200,000 international visitors (p11).

Wesgro should connect community product to the demand it already moves, and leave the building of selling bodies to municipalities, LTOs and the communities themselves. The plan's model has three parts: a selling capability that works, a link to demand that already exists and gates that must be passed before activation and investment (SME and Community Inclusion Plan, Sep 2026, p32). Two or three pilot communities test it, and it scales only after agreed thresholds are met (p32). The plan's sequence runs from validating the offer and opening a booking route, through a safety plan and a fixed-date test, to investment after demand and scale through channels (p31).

rows: Put pilot community product into the itineraries, calendars and channels Wesgro already runs, such as the Langa and Kayamandi routes and the Mal'va festival listing
Choose the two or three pilots with partners on the plan's readiness criteria, and keep the record of bookings, visitors and locally retained revenue
Form or fund a local selling body in each pilot community, with one live booking route, published dates and a named customer contact
Attach maintenance and marketing covenants to public assets before any re-letting or upgrade
Commit SAPS to the launch safety plans the pilots need, and open ACSA and other national procurement to businesses trading inside the communities

blocks.text: Kenya writes community participation into its tourism governance and investment system through community conservancies, with benefits across rural communities among the listed outcomes (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p33). The plan's own cases carry the figures: Medellín's Comuna 13 drew 1.98 million visitors in 2025 around resident-run product, while Kliptown shows what capital before an operator buys (SME and Community Inclusion Plan, Sep 2026, p8, p11).

**Initiative I12**, community inclusion pilots (section 4.3), with booking routes shared with **I3** (focus area 3). **Indicators** T1-07 community share of foreign direct spend at impact level and T2-17 communities with a live booking route at outcome level (section 5.2).
